questions.question: What is JavaScript?
questions.explanation: JavaScript is a programming language commonly used to make websites interactive.

questions.question: Which keyword creates a variable that can be reassigned?
questions.explanation: The let keyword creates a variable whose value can be changed later.

questions.question: Which method adds an item to the end of an array?
questions.explanation: push() adds one or more items to the end of an array.

questions.question: Which keyword declares a constant?
questions.explanation: const creates a variable binding that cannot be reassigned.

questions.question: Which symbol is used for strict equality?
questions.explanation: The === operator checks both value and data type.

questions.question: What is React?
questions.explanation: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces.

questions.question: Which hook is commonly used to manage state?
questions.explanation: useState allows a React component to store and update state.

questions.question: What is a React component?
questions.explanation: Components are reusable pieces of a React user interface.

questions.question: What is used to pass data from a parent to a child component?
questions.explanation: Props allow a parent component to pass data to a child component.

questions.question: Which hook is commonly used for side effects?
questions.explanation: useEffect is used to perform side effects such as API requests.

questions.question: Which HTML element creates a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The anchor element <a> creates hyperlinks.

questions.question: Which element is used for the main heading?
questions.explanation: The h1 element represents the most important heading on a page.

questions.question: Which HTML element creates a form?
questions.explanation: The form element groups controls used to collect user input.

questions.question: Which element creates a numbered list?
questions.explanation: The ol element creates an ordered, numbered list.

questions.question: Which attribute provides alternative text for an image?
questions.explanation: The alt attribute provides alternative text for images.

questions.question: Which CSS property creates a flex container?
questions.explanation: display: flex turns an element into a flex container.

questions.question: Which CSS property changes text color?
questions.explanation: The color property controls the color of text.

questions.question: Which CSS property changes the background color?
questions.explanation: background-color sets the background color of an element.

questions.question: Which layout system is useful for two-dimensional layouts?
questions.explanation: CSS Grid is designed for two-dimensional row and column layouts.

questions.question: Which unit is relative to the root font size?
questions.explanation: The rem unit is relative to the root HTML element's font size.

questions.question: What is JavaScript?
questions.description: JavaScript is widely used to add logic and interactivity to web applications.
questions.explanation: JavaScript is a programming language used to create dynamic and interactive web pages.

questions.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned?
questions.description: The let keyword is commonly used when a variable's value needs to change.
questions.explanation: let declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned later.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to declare a constant?
questions.description: Constants are useful when a variable should not be reassigned.
questions.explanation: const creates a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned.

questions.question: Which operator checks both value and data type?
questions.description: Strict equality is useful when both the value and type must match.
questions.explanation: The === operator compares two values without performing type conversion.

questions.question: Which method adds an element to the end of an array?
questions.description: Array methods allow JavaScript programs to modify collections of data.
questions.explanation: push() adds one or more elements to the end of an array.

questions.question: Which method removes the last element from an array?
questions.description: The pop method is used when the last array element needs to be removed.
questions.explanation: pop() removes and returns the last element of an array.

questions.question: Which method removes the first element from an array?
questions.description: The shift method operates on the beginning of an array.
questions.explanation: shift() removes and returns the first element of an array.

questions.question: Which method converts a JSON string into a JavaScript object?
questions.description: JSON.parse is commonly used when receiving JSON data from an API.
questions.explanation: JSON.parse() converts a valid JSON string into a JavaScript value or object.

questions.question: Which method converts a JavaScript object into a JSON string?
questions.description: JSON.stringify is useful when sending JavaScript data to a server.
questions.explanation: JSON.stringify() converts a JavaScript value into a JSON-formatted string.

questions.question: Which symbol starts a single-line comment in JavaScript?
questions.description: Comments help developers explain code without affecting execution.
questions.explanation: Two forward slashes introduce a single-line JavaScript comment.

questions.question: Which function prints a value to the browser console?
questions.description: Developers commonly use the console to inspect values and debug applications.
questions.explanation: console.log() writes information to the browser's developer console.

questions.question: Which value represents the absence of an assigned value?
questions.description: JavaScript uses undefined when a variable has not been assigned a value.
questions.explanation: A variable declared without an assigned value normally has the value undefined.

questions.question: Which method creates a new array by transforming every element?
questions.description: map is useful for transforming data before displaying it.
questions.explanation: map() returns a new array containing the results of calling a function for each element.

questions.question: Which method creates a new array containing elements that pass a test?
questions.description: Filtering is useful when only certain items from a collection are required.
questions.explanation: filter() returns a new array containing elements that satisfy a condition.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to define a function?
questions.description: Functions group reusable JavaScript instructions.
questions.explanation: The function keyword is used to declare a traditional JavaScript function.

questions.question: What does DOM stand for?
questions.description: The DOM represents the structure of a web page as objects.
questions.explanation: DOM stands for Document Object Model and allows scripts to interact with HTML elements.

questions.question: Which operator is used for logical AND?
questions.description: Logical operators are used to combine or modify conditions.
questions.explanation: The && operator returns true when both conditions are truthy.

questions.question: Which operator is used for logical OR?
questions.description: The OR operator allows a condition to succeed when at least one expression is truthy.
questions.explanation: The || operator evaluates to a truthy value when either operand is truthy.

questions.question: Which keyword returns a value from a function?
questions.description: Functions can return calculated or processed data to the calling code.
questions.explanation: The return statement ends a function and optionally provides a value.

questions.question: Which array property gives the number of elements?
questions.description: The length property is frequently used when working with arrays.
questions.explanation: The length property returns the number of elements in an array.

questions.question: What is React?
questions.description: React is used to build modern interactive user interfaces.
questions.explanation: React is a JavaScript library for building component-based user interfaces.

questions.question: What is a React component?
questions.description: Components help divide an application into smaller reusable parts.
questions.explanation: A React component is a reusable piece of the user interface.

questions.question: Which hook is used to manage state?
questions.description: State stores information that can change during the lifetime of a component.
questions.explanation: useState lets a functional component store and update state.

questions.question: Which hook is commonly used for side effects?
questions.description: API calls and other side effects are commonly handled with useEffect.
questions.explanation: useEffect lets a component perform side effects after rendering.

questions.question: How does a parent component pass data to a child?
questions.description: Props allow components to communicate from parent to child.
questions.explanation: Props are values passed from a parent component to a child component.

questions.question: Which syntax is commonly used to write HTML-like UI in React?
questions.description: JSX makes React UI code easier to read and write.
questions.explanation: JSX is a syntax extension that allows HTML-like markup inside JavaScript.

questions.question: Which attribute helps React identify list items?
questions.description: Keys help React efficiently update lists when data changes.
questions.explanation: The key prop gives React a stable identity for each list element.

questions.question: Which event is used when a button is clicked?
questions.description: React uses event handler props to respond to user interactions.
questions.explanation: onClick is the standard React event handler for click events.

questions.question: What is controlled form input in React?
options: An input controlled by JSON Server
An input controlled only by CSS
An input controlled by React state
questions.answer: An input controlled by React state
questions.description: Controlled inputs make form values available through component state.
questions.explanation: A controlled input gets its value from React state and updates through an event handler.

questions.question: Which hook can store a mutable value without causing a re-render?
questions.description: useRef is useful for DOM references and persistent mutable values.
questions.explanation: Changing a ref's current value does not by itself trigger a component re-render.

questions.question: What does React Router provide?
questions.description: React Router allows a React application to contain multiple routes or pages.
questions.explanation: React Router manages navigation between different views in a React application.

questions.question: Which method is commonly used to render an array of components?
questions.description: Mapping data into JSX is a common React pattern.
questions.explanation: Array map() can transform each item into a React element.

questions.question: What happens when React state is updated?
questions.description: State updates allow the interface to respond to changing data.
questions.explanation: Updating state schedules a re-render so React can update the UI.

questions.question: Which hook is useful for memoizing an expensive calculation?
questions.description: Memoization can prevent unnecessary recalculation of expensive values.
questions.explanation: useMemo memoizes a calculated value until its dependencies change.

questions.question: What is lifting state up?
options: Moving shared state to a common parent
questions.answer: Moving shared state to a common parent
questions.description: Lifting state helps sibling components share information.
questions.explanation: State can be moved to the closest common parent so multiple children can access it through props.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a React Fragment?
options: Group elements without adding an extra DOM element
questions.answer: Group elements without adding an extra DOM element
questions.description: Fragments help return multiple elements without unnecessary wrapper elements.
questions.explanation: React Fragment lets components group multiple children without creating an extra DOM node.

questions.question: Which file commonly contains the root React rendering code in a Vite project?
questions.description: Vite React projects commonly use main.jsx as the entry point.
questions.explanation: main.jsx typically renders the root React component into the HTML root element.

questions.question: What is conditional rendering?
options: Showing UI based on a condition
questions.answer: Showing UI based on a condition
questions.description: Conditional rendering lets the interface change according to application state.
questions.explanation: React can render different elements depending on JavaScript conditions.

questions.question: Which package can be used to make HTTP requests in a React project?
questions.description: Axios is commonly used to communicate with REST APIs.
questions.explanation: Axios is an HTTP client that can send GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE requests.

questions.question: What is a common way to fetch API data when a component loads?
questions.description: Fetching data when a component loads is a common React application pattern.
questions.explanation: useEffect can run an API request after the component renders.

questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.description: HTML provides the structure and content of web pages.
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language and is used to structure web documents.

questions.question: Which element creates the main heading?
questions.description: Heading elements provide a hierarchy for page content.
questions.explanation: The h1 element represents the highest-level heading on a page.

questions.question: Which element creates a hyperlink?
questions.description: Links allow users to navigate between pages and resources.
questions.explanation: The anchor element creates hyperlinks, usually using the href attribute.

questions.question: Which attribute specifies the destination of a link?
questions.description: The href attribute tells the browser where a hyperlink should lead.
questions.explanation: href specifies the URL or destination of an anchor element.

questions.question: Which element displays an image?
questions.description: Images are embedded in HTML using the img element.
questions.explanation: The img element embeds an image into an HTML document.

questions.question: Which attribute provides alternative text for an image?
questions.description: Alternative text improves accessibility and provides information when an image cannot load.
questions.explanation: The alt attribute provides a text alternative for an image.

questions.question: Which element creates an unordered list?
questions.description: Unordered lists are normally displayed with bullet points.
questions.explanation: The ul element creates an unordered list.

questions.question: Which element creates an ordered list?
questions.description: Ordered lists are useful when the order of items matters.
questions.explanation: The ol element creates a numbered or ordered list.

questions.question: Which element represents a list item?
questions.description: The li element represents an individual item inside a list.
questions.explanation: The li element defines a list item inside ul or ol.

questions.question: Which element creates a form?
questions.description: Forms collect information from users.
questions.explanation: The form element groups controls used to collect and submit user input.

questions.question: Which input type is used for an email address?
questions.description: The email input type provides semantic information and browser validation.
questions.explanation: input type=email is designed for entering email addresses.

questions.question: Which element creates a button?
questions.description: Buttons are commonly used to trigger actions.
questions.explanation: The button element creates a clickable button in HTML.

questions.question: Which semantic element represents navigation links?
questions.description: Semantic elements make the structure of a page clearer.
questions.explanation: The nav element represents a section containing navigation links.

questions.question: Which element represents the main content of a document?
questions.description: The main element identifies the primary content of the document.
questions.explanation: The main element represents the dominant content of the body.

questions.question: Which element defines a paragraph?
questions.description: Paragraphs are used to organize blocks of written content.
questions.explanation: The p element represents a paragraph.

questions.question: Which element contains metadata about an HTML document?
questions.description: The head contains information used by the browser and other tools.
questions.explanation: The head element contains metadata, title, stylesheets and other document information.

questions.question: Which element contains the visible page content?
questions.description: The body contains the content displayed in the browser window.
questions.explanation: The body element contains the document's visible content.

questions.question: Which HTML attribute makes an input required?
questions.description: Required fields help ensure important information is provided.
questions.explanation: The required attribute tells the browser that a form control must have a value before submission.

questions.question: Which element is commonly used for a table row?
questions.description: HTML tables are organized into rows and cells.
questions.explanation: The tr element defines a row in an HTML table.

questions.question: Which element defines a table data cell?
questions.description: Table data cells contain individual pieces of table information.
questions.explanation: The td element defines a standard data cell in a table row.

questions.question: What does CSS stand for?
questions.description: CSS controls the appearance and layout of web pages.
questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets and is used to style HTML elements.

questions.question: Which property changes text color?
questions.description: The color property controls the foreground text color.
questions.explanation: The CSS color property sets the color of text.

questions.question: Which property changes the background color?
questions.description: Background colors help visually separate and organize sections.
questions.explanation: background-color sets the background color of an element.

questions.question: Which declaration creates a flex container?
questions.description: Flexbox is useful for arranging items in rows or columns.
questions.explanation: display:flex turns an element into a flex container.

questions.question: Which layout system is designed for rows and columns?
questions.description: CSS Grid is useful for two-dimensional layouts.
questions.explanation: CSS Grid provides a row-and-column based layout system.

questions.question: Which property controls the space inside an element?
questions.description: Padding creates space between content and an element's border.
questions.explanation: The padding property controls the inner spacing of an element.

questions.question: Which property controls the space outside an element?
questions.description: Margins create space between an element and surrounding elements.
questions.explanation: The margin property controls the outer spacing of an element.

questions.question: Which property changes the font size?
questions.description: Font size controls how large text appears.
questions.explanation: The font-size property specifies the size of text.

questions.question: Which property makes text bold?
questions.description: Font weight controls the thickness of text.
questions.explanation: font-weight can be set to values such as bold or 700.

questions.question: Which property controls the width of an element?
questions.description: The width property controls an element's horizontal size.
questions.explanation: CSS width specifies the width of an element's box.

questions.question: Which property controls the height of an element?
questions.description: Height controls the vertical size of an element.
questions.explanation: The height property specifies the height of an element.

questions.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the root font size?
questions.description: rem is useful for scalable and consistent typography.
questions.explanation: One rem is based on the font size of the root HTML element.

questions.question: Which unit is relative to the viewport height?
questions.description: Viewport units are useful for responsive layouts.
questions.explanation: 1vh represents 1 percent of the viewport height.

questions.question: Which unit is relative to the viewport width?
questions.description: vw can be used when an element should scale with viewport width.
questions.explanation: 1vw represents 1 percent of the viewport width.

questions.question: Which property rounds the corners of an element?
questions.description: Rounded corners are commonly used in modern UI design.
questions.explanation: border-radius controls the rounding of an element's corners.

questions.question: Which property controls the alignment of flex items along the main axis?
questions.description: Flexbox provides properties for controlling item alignment.
questions.explanation: justify-content controls distribution of flex items along the main axis.

questions.question: Which property controls alignment on the cross axis in flexbox?
questions.description: align-items is commonly used to vertically align items in a row flex container.
questions.explanation: align-items controls alignment of flex items on the cross axis.

questions.question: Which CSS feature is commonly used for responsive design?
questions.description: Responsive websites adapt their layout to different screen sizes.
questions.explanation: CSS media queries apply styles based on conditions such as viewport width.

questions.question: Which property controls whether an element is displayed?
questions.description: The display property controls an element's layout behavior and visibility.
questions.explanation: display:none removes an element from the normal layout.

questions.question: Which property controls the stacking order of positioned elements?
questions.description: z-index is useful when elements overlap.
questions.explanation: z-index controls the stacking order of positioned elements.
